You are building a narrow, injectable OBSERVATION VERIFIER in freytag-forge (Python 3.12), to be run in SHADOW only (it never changes a turn). Working directory: /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge. export PYTHONPATH=/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge TMPDIR=/tmp CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_URL=https://w.example; run `.venv/bin/python`. No network, no live model call, no uv. Do not git commit. NEVER print or write any credential. NO regular expressions. No story vocabulary (no Kristin, truck, laptop, drawer, Michelle) in non-test code; tests may use invented generic names. YOU MAY EDIT ONLY: new storygame/runtime/observation_verifier.py and new tests/test_observation_verifier.py. Read first: storygame/runtime/observation.py (ObservationContext, ObservedThing), storygame/runtime/jev.py (JevClient.ask(state, questions) -> dict|None; noul_yes; THRESHOLD), storygame/runtime/jev_questions.py (question shape: {key: {type:'noul', instructions, criteria:{true,false}}}, and `_answer`), docs/jev-guard-rules.md (short fact questions only; 'yes' always means the thing you look for; one sentence role line helps; code does the comparing), and the verifier section of .plans/grounded-llm-environment-narration.md (search 'Check prose, not the model').

PURPOSE: given the FINAL displayed narration and the required relations of an ObservationContext, ask Jev ONE batched request (one question per relation) whether the narration actually describes each named thing, as present now, at its permitted place or holder. A thing that is only named is not enough: 'the X is missing', 'if the X were here', 'she remembers the X on the shelf', X in a different place or held by someone else, and X not mentioned at all must all be 'no'. Do not try to detect unreported inventions (Jev cannot); do not ask 'did it invent anything'.

API TO BUILD (exact names; later tasks import them):
- `@dataclass(frozen=True) class Relation: thing: str; place: str | None = None; holder: str | None = None`
- `relations_from_context(context: ObservationContext) -> tuple[Relation, ...]`: one Relation per name in context.required, taking place/holder from the matching ObservedThing in context.visible_things (match by name); a required name with no matching visible thing yields Relation(thing=name) with no place/holder. Deterministic order = context.required order.
- `@dataclass(frozen=True) class RelationVerdict: relation: Relation; verdict: str; score: float | None` with verdict one of 'accept', 'reject', 'uncertain', 'unavailable'.
- `@dataclass(frozen=True) class VerifierReport: verdicts: tuple[RelationVerdict, ...]; outcome: str; requests: int; elapsed_s: float; failure: str | None` with outcome one of 'ok', 'partial', 'unavailable', 'malformed', 'budget_exhausted', 'no_relations'. Property `accepted -> bool` is True only when outcome == 'ok' and EVERY verdict is 'accept' (unknown, uncertain, timeout all fail closed). `failure` is a short generic code (for example 'ask_returned_none', 'no_valid_answers', 'missing_answer:<index>', 'request_budget') and NEVER contains narration text, thing names from the narration, or model output.
- `class ObservationVerifier`: `__init__(self, ask, *, accept_above=0.65, reject_below=0.35, max_requests_per_turn=2, clock=time.monotonic)` where `ask(state, questions) -> dict | None` is the same callable shape as JevClient.ask (inject it; the class never builds a client or reads the environment); validate 0 <= reject_below < accept_above <= 1; `begin_turn()` resets the per-turn request counter; `verify(narration: str, relations: Sequence[Relation]) -> VerifierReport`. No relations -> outcome 'no_relations', zero requests. If the per-turn budget is spent -> outcome 'budget_exhausted', zero requests, no ask call. Otherwise exactly ONE ask call: state = {'narration': narration}, questions = one noul question per relation under keys 'relation_0', 'relation_1', ... Each question's instructions open with a single role sentence (a continuity editor for an interactive story), name the thing and its place or holder in the text, say the narration must show the thing there as a present fact, and say it is NOT shown when it is missing, only imagined, remembered, denied, elsewhere, with someone else, or not mentioned; criteria.true / criteria.false state the same. Score = answers[key]['noul'] when it is a real number (not bool) in [0,1]; verdict accept if score > accept_above, reject if score < reject_below, else uncertain; a missing or non-numeric answer -> verdict 'unavailable' with score None. ask returning None or raising -> outcome 'unavailable' with every verdict 'unavailable' (never let an exception escape verify). If every answer is invalid -> 'malformed'; some valid, some not -> 'partial'. Count the request in `requests` and the per-turn counter even when it fails. `elapsed_s` is measured with the injected clock around the ask call.
- `class_attribute`/constant `QUESTION_VERSION = 'observation-relation-v1'` so a corpus run can record which wording was scored.

TESTS FIRST in tests/test_observation_verifier.py (pure, hermetic, fake `ask`; see them fail, then implement). Cover: relations_from_context on a hand-built ObservationContext (place case, holder case, missing visible thing, order); one batched ask call with N questions for N relations and the narration in state; accept/reject/uncertain at and around both thresholds (equality is uncertain); ask None -> unavailable; ask raising -> unavailable without raising; answer missing one key -> partial + 'unavailable' verdict for that relation; every answer malformed -> malformed; bool or string noul -> unavailable; per-turn budget (third verify in a turn with max 2 -> budget_exhausted and the fake ask is not called; begin_turn resets); no relations -> no_relations and no call; `accepted` false for any non-accept; failure codes contain none of the narration text; invalid threshold arguments raise ValueError; question text contains the thing name and place/holder and the word 'narration'. Keep the file focused: no duplicate cases.

FINISH: ruff check and ruff format the two files; report pass counts and quote the final `verify` method.

You are an author of LABELLED TEST CASES for a narration verifier in freytag-forge. Working directory: /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge. export PYTHONPATH=/home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge TMPDIR=/tmp CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_URL=https://w.example; run `.venv/bin/python`. No network, no live model call, no uv. Do not git commit. NEVER print or write any credential. YOU MAY WRITE ONLY ONE NEW FILE: scripts/ringer/environment_narration/verifier_corpus/cases-a.jsonl (create the directory if needed). Do not edit any other file.

WHAT THE VERIFIER DOES: it reads a short piece of story narration plus one or more RELATIONS, each 'THING is at PLACE' or 'THING is held by HOLDER', and answers yes/no per relation: does the narration actually show that thing there, as a present fact? You are writing the ground truth it will be scored against, so every label must be unarguable to a careful human reader.

WRITE exactly 56 cases for these stories: a Victorian country-house mystery and a space-station maintenance story. Use about 28 per story, with fresh character, place and object names (invent them; the narration is plain third-person prose, 2 to 5 sentences, 25 to 90 words, in the style of a game narrator answering a player's look/search/enter command). One JSON object per line (JSONL), fields exactly: {"id": "a-001", "story": short story label, "category": one of the categories below, "narration": text, "relations": [{"thing": name as a short noun phrase, "place": container/surface/room name or null, "holder": a character name or null, "label": "accept" or "reject"}], "undetectable_invention": true/false, "note": one sentence saying why the label is right}. A relation has place OR holder (not both), except at most 4 relations in the file may have both null (meaning 'present in the scene'). `thing`, `place` and `holder` are the plain names an engine would store (for example 'brass key', 'the writing desk'); the narration may paraphrase them.

CATEGORIES (label rules; every case is one category; aim for about 5 or 6 cases of each in your file, and keep reject relations between 45% and 55% of all relations):
- positive_plain: the narration names the thing at the stated place/holder in ordinary words. accept.
- positive_paraphrase: same truth, but the thing and/or place are described in different words ('the seat beside her' for 'passenger seat'; 'a slim leather book' for 'journal'), still clearly the same thing. accept.
- negated: the narration names the thing but says it is gone, missing, not there, or was never there. reject.
- hypothetical_or_remembered: the thing is only wished for, feared, rumoured, remembered, promised or conditional ('if the key were on the hook'). reject.
- wrong_holder: the narration clearly puts the thing in a different character's hands than the relation says. reject.
- wrong_place: the narration clearly puts the thing in a different place than the relation says (a different container, room or seat). reject.
- not_mentioned: the narration is about the right scene but never mentions the thing at all. reject.
- lookalike_substitute: the narration shows a DIFFERENT but similar thing at the place (a paper note where the relation says ledger; a silver spoon where it says silver key). reject.
- invention_unreported: the thing IS correctly shown at its place (relation label accept), but the narration also invents an extra clue, object or fact that is not in any relation. Set undetectable_invention true on these. accept.
- multi_mixed: 2 or 3 relations in one narration, with a mix of accept and reject labels, each independently true. Per-relation labels.
Set undetectable_invention false everywhere else. Make about 40 percent of the cases MINIMAL PAIRS: write an accept narration and, on a different id, a near-copy that changes one fact so the relation becomes reject (and vice versa); pairs must sit in different categories where that is natural. Vary the sentence structure, the length, the order in which the thing appears (first sentence, last sentence, buried), whether the thing is the focus or incidental, and keep reject cases subtle, not obviously absurd. Do not reuse the same thing name in more than 3 cases. Never put an instruction, a label or a hint about the answer into the narration itself. Do not copy these instruction examples verbatim.

SELF-CHECK before you finish: re-read every case once as a skeptical human and fix any label you could argue against; remove ambiguity instead of keeping it. Then run the python check in your task's final line (it validates structure only) and report the category counts and the reject share.
tasks.check:
cd /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge && .venv/bin/python - <<'PY'
import json,sys,collections
cats=['positive_plain', 'positive_paraphrase', 'negated', 'hypothetical_or_remembered', 'wrong_holder', 'wrong_place', 'not_mentioned', 'lookalike_substitute', 'invention_unreported', 'multi_mixed']
p='scripts/ringer/environment_narration/verifier_corpus/cases-a.jsonl'
rows=[json.loads(l) for l in open(p,encoding='utf-8') if l.strip()]
assert len(rows)==56, 'need exactly 56 cases, got %d'%len(rows)
ids=[r['id'] for r in rows]; assert len(set(ids))==56 and all(i.startswith('a-') for i in ids), 'ids'
cc=collections.Counter(); lab=collections.Counter(); both=0
for r in rows:
    assert set(r)=={'id','story','category','narration','relations','undetectable_invention','note'}, ('fields',r['id'])
    assert r['category'] in cats, ('category',r['id'])
    n=len(r['narration'].split()); assert 15<=n<=110, ('length',r['id'],n)
    assert isinstance(r['undetectable_invention'],bool) and r['undetectable_invention']==(r['category']=='invention_unreported'), ('flag',r['id'])
    assert 1<=len(r['relations'])<=3 and (len(r['relations'])>1)==(r['category']=='multi_mixed'), ('relcount',r['id'])
    cc[r['category']]+=1
    for x in r['relations']:
        assert set(x)=={'thing','place','holder','label'} and x['label'] in ('accept','reject'), ('rel',r['id'])
        assert x['thing'].strip() and not (x['place'] and x['holder']), ('placeholder',r['id'])
        both+= (x['place'] is None and x['holder'] is None)
        lab[x['label']]+=1
        c=r['category']
        if c in ('positive_plain','positive_paraphrase','invention_unreported'): assert x['label']=='accept', ('label',r['id'])
        if c in ('negated','hypothetical_or_remembered','wrong_holder','wrong_place','not_mentioned','lookalike_substitute'): assert x['label']=='reject', ('label',r['id'])
    if r['category']=='multi_mixed': assert {x['label'] for x in r['relations']}=={'accept','reject'}, ('mixed',r['id'])
assert all(cc[c]>=4 for c in cats), ('category counts',dict(cc))
tot=sum(lab.values()); share=lab['reject']/tot; assert 0.45<=share<=0.55, ('reject share',share)
assert both<=4, 'too many null/null relations'
banned=['kristin','michelle','brandon','laptop','truck','drawer','memory card']
text=open(p,encoding='utf-8').read().lower()
assert not any(b in text for b in banned), 'product vocabulary used'
print('corpus ok', dict(cc), dict(lab))
PY
